skill.name: gwas-database
skill.description: Query the NHGRI-EBI GWAS Catalog for SNP-trait associations, studies, variants, genes, traits, p-values, effect sizes, and summary statistics workflows.
skill.summary: Query GWAS Catalog associations, variants, traits, studies, and summary statistics.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The command-execution findings in SKILL.md are Markdown backticks and code fences, not executable Ruby or shell invocations. Most network findings are expected documentation for public NHGRI-EBI GWAS Catalog endpoints. The actionable risks are plaintext FTP or HTTP download guidance and an example that writes downloaded files without path validation.

remediation.issue: Plaintext FTP or HTTP download examples
remediation.suggestion: Prefer HTTPS endpoints where available, document checksum verification, and avoid shell download commands for untrusted inputs.

remediation.issue: Downloaded file path is built from function arguments
remediation.suggestion: Validate GCST identifiers, normalize output paths, reject path separators, and avoid overwriting existing files without confirmation.

static_findings.snippet: - Avoid hammering the API with rapid consecutive requests
- Variant IDs: `rs` numbers (e.g., rs7903146) or `variant_id` format
- `size` parameter: Number of results per page
- `_links` in response: URLs for next/previous pages
The web interface at https://www.ebi.ac.uk/gwas/ supports multiple search modes:

content.value_statement: Genetic researchers need reliable access to curated SNP-trait associations and summary statistics. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through GWAS Catalog searches and API workflows.
actual_capabilities: Find GWAS Catalog endpoints for studies, variants, traits, genes, and associations.
Build REST API queries for rs IDs, EFO traits, genomic regions, and GCST studies.
Interpret common fields such as p-values, effect sizes, risk alleles, ancestry, and sample size.
Guide summary statistics access through the API, web interface, or public download locations.
Suggest workflows for systematic reviews, variant lookup, gene analysis, and polygenic score research.
limitations: It does not provide medical advice or clinical genetic interpretation.
It depends on public GWAS Catalog availability and current endpoint behavior.
It does not guarantee that every study has full summary statistics.
Users must verify findings against original publications before reporting results.

use_cases.title: Review disease associations
use_cases.description: Find variants, p-values, effect sizes, and source studies for a disease or phenotype.

use_cases.title: Inspect a candidate variant
use_cases.description: Summarize known trait associations for a specific rs ID and compare reported evidence.

use_cases.title: Plan a systematic evidence search
use_cases.description: Create a reproducible GWAS Catalog query strategy with trait terms, filters, and citation notes.

prompt_templates.title: Look Up A Variant
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the GWAS Catalog skill to summarize known trait associations for rs7903146. Include traits, p-values, effect sizes, and study identifiers when available.

prompt_templates.title: Find Trait Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Find GWAS Catalog evidence for type 2 diabetes. Use the relevant EFO trait when possible and list genome-wide significant associations with study context.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Gene Associations
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the GWAS Catalog skill to investigate variants near TCF7L2. Group associations by trait and note p-values, effect sizes, and population details.

prompt_templates.title: Design A Reproducible Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a reproducible plan to collect all type 2 diabetes associations from the GWAS Catalog. Include p-value filters, pagination, access dates, and a summary table.

output_examples.output: A concise summary listing associated traits, strongest p-values, risk alleles, study accessions, and notes about replication evidence.

output_examples.input: Create a GWAS Catalog query plan for body mass index.
output_examples.output: A step-by-step workflow with trait selection, endpoint choice, pagination guidance, significance filters, and citation reminders.

output_examples.input: Compare GWAS evidence for variants near APOE.
output_examples.output: A research-focused comparison of nearby variants, reported traits, study metadata, ancestry context, and interpretation cautions.

best_practices: Record the GWAS Catalog access date and cite both Catalog and original studies.
Use EFO identifiers when possible to avoid ambiguous trait names.
Check ancestry, sample size, and replication status before comparing associations.
anti_patterns: Do not treat GWAS associations as clinical recommendations.
Do not mix effect sizes from different studies without harmonizing alleles and populations.
Do not run bulk downloads repeatedly when one cached dataset is sufficient.

faq.question: What database does this skill use?
faq.answer: It focuses on the public NHGRI-EBI GWAS Catalog and its REST and summary statistics APIs.

faq.question: Can it search by rs ID?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides workflows for looking up variants by rs ID and reviewing related trait associations.

faq.question: Can it search by disease or trait?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides searches by trait names and EFO identifiers when those identifiers are available.

faq.question: Does it provide clinical advice?
faq.answer: No. It supports research workflows and does not provide diagnosis, treatment, or clinical risk advice.

faq.question: Does every study include summary statistics?
faq.answer: No. Full summary statistics are available only for studies that have deposited that data.

faq.question: What tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
